verdicts.label: T4
verdicts.reason: The line runs across the full width. The summit of the dominant left-centre mountain (x≈483) sits on the photo's rounded summit, and the left ridge (y≈335–345) lies on the real skyline. In the middle, the line hugs the dark jagged peaks and the dip near x≈1050, and on the right it follows the ridge up to the right edge with no visible offset or tilt.

verdicts.label: P2
verdicts.reason: The Legnone bump (x≈707) lines up with the distant pyramid in the centre of the photo (≈720). The rise at Termine Quadro follows the right-hand dark ridge up to the right edge. The line sits about 1–1.4% of image height above the real ridge at the left and right ends and is closer in the middle, so the offset is even with no tilt, but that margin is close to the 1.5% limit.

verdicts.label: R6
verdicts.reason: This is effectively the same overlay as P2 (the Legnone and Termine Quadro positions match after scaling). The Legnone bump sits on the central distant pyramid, and the right section follows the near dark ridge, with only a small, even vertical offset close to the limit.

verdicts.label: E4
verdicts.reason: Same peak set as P2, but shifted left: the Legnone bump is at x≈486 while the real pyramid is at ≈720. The line climbs to the right ridge too early (around x≈880–1070) and runs above the real ridgelines in the centre.

verdicts.label: E9
verdicts.reason: Same terrain shifted right: the Legnone bump is at x≈900 while the real pyramid is at ≈720, and the line is missing over the left ~20% of the frame. On the right it dips to y≈150 and cuts across the slope of the dark mountain instead of following its ridge.

verdicts.label: D5
verdicts.reason: The labels come from a different view direction (Camoghè, Gazzirola, Monte Bar, Adula to the north). The line runs along the very top of the frame, well above the real skyline, and has no bump at the central distant pyramid.
